input.objective: Launch PLEA test run 6 on Sepolia from this Foundry repository exactly as launch.json lists it: five contracts (PLEA, CabalGate, Seasons, PleaDistributor, PleaLaunch), deployed in order in one transaction with the constructor arguments in launch.json. The code is test run 5's (job e0891351, same contracts; that job stalled in your adapt step on machine errors and seat timeouts, so this run repeats it with build guidance): run 4's deployed code (launch #1466, adb9f44) plus a fix round and Objection!. Fix round: an APPEAL letter of a floor-sized plea is raised to the 0.70 IMD floor instead of refused (capped at the original amount and 50% of the balance), Seasons also excludes the launch owner read from the hook's owner() with a non-reverting staticcall (a pending two-step owner is deliberately not excluded), the appeal question states the real previous score and need, and CabalGate.DEFINITIONS v3 adds that naming the earlier verdict in an appeal is not manipulation; keep the definitions text exactly as it is. New: Objection! (src/Tribunal.sol, spec OBJECTIONS.md; ownerless; deployed after the launch through PleaLaunch.deployTribunal(creationCode) against the keccak256 committed as PleaLaunch's 13th argument, zero meaning no objections). For 20 minutes after an approval anyone except the seller and the wallets Seasons excludes may object: 1-280 bytes under the gate's text rules plus no [OBJECTION markers, the 0.5 IMD oracle fee (minted on Sepolia, like the Letterbox's) and a 0.35 IMD stake in pool IMD. The Tribunal asks Intake v2 with requestWithFailure using the gate's body parameters, the gate's own question verbatim plus the original score and the objection as untrusted text, and the gate's five definitions verbatim plus one objection member (version 2, calibrated with ten live Sepolia panels); it verifies attestations under its own EIP-712 domain with the gate's signer and stores only. Sustained when newScore + 2 < need (no points this season, stake back); otherwise overruled (stake to Seasons' pot through settle); a refused or split panel or 20 minutes without a ruling voids it (stake back). The recorded score is the lowest any panel gave, never above the original; at most two rulings per plea from different wallets, a sustain closes the case, one pending objection at a time. Seasons.record refuses a held plea (window open or objection pending) and a sustained one; closeSeason skips them; Seasons reads the Tribunal through PLEA's launcher with non-reverting staticcalls, so with no Tribunal nothing changes; window plus expiry (40 minutes) end inside the 1-hour close grace (tested). The sale is never touched and rulings never reset the dead-man. Numbers: PLEA.init mints 82% to the hook, 6% to Seasons and 12% to PleaDistributor (the swarm's 10% and a 2% airdrop, one Merkle root); the PLEA bonus is 10,000,000 PLEA for each of the first six seasons; Seasons pays the top 25 wallets with 60 or more points shares from 450 down to 350 basis points in a straight line (Seasons.shareBps, 10,000 in all) for the IMD pot and the bonus alike; the Letterbox leaderboard lists 25 ranks and its status line shows held, pending, lowered and sustained points. Everything else is run 4's as you deployed it (letters, APPEAL, SELL and NAME, auto-sell with the 0.35 IMD fee never more than the sale and the 0.25 IMD tip, the trader rule in PleaHook, no keeper tip, Ownable2Step, share bands 18/11/5 at 20%/35%, no Laureates). Build: the whole tree compiles under via_ir (two contracts sit near the size limit); the five sources build in under a minute, the 63 test files take about 16 minutes more on 4 cores, so run forge build --skip test --skip script first, then the tests in groups with forge test --match-path (each group compiles only its own files; the fork tests skip without SEPOLIA_RPC_URL / MAINNET_RPC_URL). test/Tribunal.t.sol, TribunalSeasons.t.sol, TribunalStanding.t.sol and TribunalAdversarial.t.sol cover the new contract; test/LaunchManifest.t.sol asserts the launch fits the 16,777,216-gas cap with your factory's 22% headroom (13.1M, 16.0M with headroom), ties launch.json to both committed code hashes and keeps its notes under the manifest's 4,000-character cap. Audit the imported code and deploy it unchanged; fix only what the audit proves is a real bug, and keep every number as it is (fees, timings, panel 30, quorum 17, 5-hour seasons, 33-hour dead-man, START 1792162800, credit gas 1300000, letters 20%, plea 1% to 50% or 2.5M, 0.70 IMD minimum plea value, 95% sale minimum, fee cap +10%, six bonus seasons of 10,000,000 PLEA, the 82/6/12 split, top 25 from 450 to 350 bps, objection window 20 minutes, stake 0.35 IMD, margin 2, two rulings per plea). If you change the Letterbox or the Tribunal, update its code hash in launch.json. Runtime sizes: CabalGate 24,376 bytes (200 under the EIP-170 limit), PleaHook 24,296 (280 under), Letterbox 22,444, Tribunal 19,645, Seasons 11,427: keep any fix within them. Keep PLEA.setLauncher accepting either the deploy-transaction flag or PLEA's deployment block, and keep foundry.toml as it is, including [lint] lint_on_build = false and the read-only fs_permissions for ./out and ./launch.json.
